brief: Doctrine rewrite of 2026-08-21: every line is about the weather; the picture is the evidence. Three lines per photograph (Al’s ruled keeps locked and counted). Bank rescues marked. PAIRING-TASTE + the swap test still bind.
linesLabel: three per image incl. locked keeps

images.seen: A cyclist with a buff over his face riding down a bare-tree suburban avenue at golden dawn, deep blue cloudless sky, long shadows across the road. Thursday.
lines: Not one cloud, not one degree: a Highveld winter morning doing both at once.
Blue overhead, ice in the air: he is dressed for the truth, not the view.
Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.

images.seen: A hadeda landing on a frosted lawn at pink dawn, breath-mist at its beak, brick double-storey with one lit kitchen window behind. Tuesday.
lines: The hadeda has landed on frost and is already drafting a complaint.
Frost on the lawn and the morning alarm has just landed, feathers and all.
The first bird down this morning found the grass crunchy and said so.

images.seen: A Karoo farmer in a leather hat leaning on a whitewashed wall in full sun, breath visible against a deep blue sky, dry veld to the horizon. Tuesday.
lines: Full sun, visible breath: the Karoo running both seasons before lunch.
That wall holds the morning's heat by ten and he knows exactly where to lean.
Sun on your back, freezer on your face.

images.seen: A father and son in school uniform getting into a white Hilux on a frosty morning, frosted windows, breath clouds, frost-grey lawn and bare trees, clear blue sky. Wednesday.
lines: Breath like smoke, frost on the glass, sun already out: Highveld school run.
The bakkie iced over under a completely clear sky, which is exactly how it works.
The sun is up and doing its best; the frost is unconvinced so far.

images.seen: A ridgeback sitting at the driveway gate at frosty dusk, breath visible, orange-to-navy clear gradient over the trees, frost on the lawn, warm window lit behind. Tuesday.
lines: Frost already forming and the sun barely down: tonight means business.
Even the guard dog's breath is showing, and the stars are not even out yet.
A clear dusk on the Highveld is just the frost clearing its throat.

images.seen: Towels frosted stiff on the washing line at orange dusk, frosted lawn and aloes, terracotta-roofed house behind. Monday.
lines: The towels went out damp and are coming in as boards.
Sunset is doing the colours; the frost is already doing the towels.
That washing is not dry; it is preserved. Winter dusk works fast out here.

images.seen: Five friends in beanies and blankets around a modern concrete fire bowl at clear dusk, mugs steaming, modern double-storey house behind. Friday.
lines: Clear sky, sharp air, one fire bowl doing the work of a whole summer.
The temperature dropped with the sun and the circle got tighter by exactly that much.
The evening turned cold the minute it turned beautiful, which is the usual trade.

images.seen: A frosted sports field at dusk with floodlights on, folded blankets on the bench, a ball on the white grass, clubhouse and orange horizon behind. Saturday.
lines: A sky that clean means the field freezes before the floodlights even warm up.
Frost on the pitch an hour after sundown — whoever trains tonight earns it.
The blankets on the bench are not decoration; the touchline is minus something.

images.seen: The Southern Cross bright in a star-packed sky over a dark house, frost-silvered long grass and a bare tree. Thursday.
lines: The Southern Cross is out and the lawn has gone silver under it.
A sky this clean at night is beautiful, and it charges in degrees.
Stars that sharp come standard with air this cold — it is a package deal.

images.seen: A man wrapped in a blanket on a rocking chair on the stoep at night, steaming mug in hand, stars over the frosty veld. Sunday.
lines: The blanket came outside because the sky was worth it, and it is.
The cold is charging admission tonight and the sky is worth every degree.
Steam off the mug, frost on the veld, stars on duty: Sunday closed properly.

images.seen: Three men in beanies and puffers around a kettle braai on a frosty patio at night, steam and smoke rising, town lights and stars beyond. Saturday.
lines: Braaiing in beanies under a hard clear sky: winter never cancelled anything here.
The stars came out for the wors, and the frost came with them.
The fire is the only thing out here allowed to take its jacket off.

images.seen: A windpomp standing dead still over frosted Karoo scrub at pink-and-blue dawn, stone dam at its base, koppies on the horizon. Saturday.
lines: Frost right up to the dam wall: the Karoo did its winter thing overnight.
Not enough wind to turn one blade, which is why the frost got everything.
Pink sky, white veld: the desert runs both extremes before breakfast.

images.seen: Frosted wheelie bins in a row at the curb at golden dawn, Cape Winelands District Municipality branding, frost on the verge, clear sky. Monday.
lines: Bin day, and the frost got to them before the truck did.
Even the bins iced over, which is the Winelands telling you to dress properly.
The municipality collects at seven; the frost delivered at four.

images.seen: A runner in a beanie pausing on a stone-walled lookout over the Joburg skyline at golden dawn, Hillbrow Tower in view, breath visible, bare winter trees below. Sunday.
lines: Joburg winter dawn: the view is free; the air charges admission.
His breath is the only cloud between here and the Hillbrow Tower.
The city looks its best exactly when the air hurts most, which is unfair.

images.seen: A mother scraping frost off the windscreen at deep blue dawn while two boys in beanies wait with their school bags, breath clouds, frosted grasses, modern house. Wednesday.
lines: The windscreen kept a record of last night and she is deleting it by hand.
Two beanies, one scraper, minus three: the school run starts before the car agrees.
The car spent the night outside under a clear sky and it shows, everywhere.

images.seen: Five guinea fowl crossing a frosty suburban street in single file at sunrise, frosted lawns and a brick house behind. Friday.
lines: Five guinea fowl crossing in single file: the frost has everyone walking carefully.
First traffic of the morning, and it walks and complains at the same time.
Frost on every lawn and the only ones out are wearing feathers.

images.seen: A boerboel basking eyes-closed against a sunny wall, faint breath vapour, water bowl beside him, dead-brown winter lawn and hard blue sky. Monday.
lines: Full sun, brown grass, visible breath: the boerboel has found the warm wall.
The sunny side of the wall is prime property, and it is taken.
The lawn went beige weeks ago; the sky never got the memo.

images.seen: A parkrun start on frosty grass — runners in beanies and gloves, breath clouds everywhere, marshals in hi-vis, brick clubhouse behind, clear pale sky. Sunday.
lines: Half the field is steam before anyone has run a step.
Frost on the grass, steam off the field: winter running weather at its most honest.
Cold enough to see every breath, clear enough that nobody minds.

images.seen: Two horses standing together in a frosty paddock at golden dusk, their breath steaming and backlit, bare trees behind. Wednesday.
lines: The horses are doing their own weather report, one breath at a time.
The frost is back on the grass before the sun is even gone.
Golden light, silver breath: a winter dusk doing both its tricks at once.

images.seen: A cat on the windowsill watching a pink-red winter sunset through a window frosting at its edges, frosty garden and mountains beyond. Sunday.
lines: The window is frosting at the edges and the cat has the best seat for it.
That sunset is happening at two degrees, which is why it is watched from inside.
Pink sky through cold glass: winter does its best work at a distance.

images.seen: A girl in a puffer jacket, beanie and basketball shorts mid-jumpshot at dusk, breath visible, frost creeping across the lawn edges, orange horizon behind a white farmhouse. Thursday.
lines: Shorts and a beanie: half of her believes the sky, half believes the air.
Free throws until the light or the temperature gives out, whichever is first.
Every shot comes with its own little cloud of breath tonight.

images.seen: A man in a puffer and beanie wheeling the bin down the driveway at night, breath clouding under the porch light, frosty lawn, stars overhead. Tuesday.
lines: Taking the bin out counts as an expedition once the frost settles in.
The bin run is being done at speed tonight, and the sky knows why.
Clear night, hard frost coming: even the bin trip earns a beanie.

images.seen: Frost-crusted cars parked down a lamplit, tree-lined street at night, stars in a clear navy sky. Monday.
lines: Every windscreen on this street is white already, and it is not even late.
The streetlights are warm-toned; nothing else out here is.
The frost is doing the rounds tonight and skipping nobody.

images.seen: A father and two kids under fleece blankets with mugs on the couch at night, the frosted garden glittering through the window under stars. Wednesday.
lines: Outside is glitter and minus three; inside is fleece and the remote.
The frost got the garden; the family got the couch. Fair trade.
Movie night moved up an hour the moment the frost showed up on the hedge.

images.seen: A couple lying under duvets in a bakkie bed, pointing up at a massive Milky Way over dark veld, flask and enamel mugs on the tailgate. Friday.
lines: Duvets in the bakkie, flask on the tailgate: the sky is worth the freeze tonight.
Winter skies are the sharp ones — the cold is the price of that many stars.
The heater is at home; the Milky Way is here; the duvet split the difference.

images.seen: Two colleagues in coats and scarves chatting over takeaway coffees in a sunlit city plaza, brilliant blue sky between the glass towers. Friday.
lines: Coats and coffees in full sun: winter in this city photographs like summer.
The sky says lunch outside; the scarves say make it a quick one.
Not a cloud between the towers, and still nobody unbuttoned anything.

images.seen: A mother zipping a grumpy toddler into a puffer jacket at the kitchen table, porridge steaming, frosty veld and blue sky through the window. Thursday.
lines: The jacket is going on because the window already said so.
Porridge steaming, veld frosted: breakfast comes with a dress code today.
The face says no; the frost outside says absolutely yes.

images.seen: An empty rugby field in the morning — frost surviving in the grandstand's shadow, sunlit golden grass, tall poles against a brilliant blue sky. Saturday.
lines: The frost only survives in the stand's shadow, and you can see the exact line.
Blue sky, gold grass, white edges: a Highveld rugby morning in full kit.
Lekker koud, but the rugby fields are about to look perfect.
